correctness.rationale: The exact fixed-coordinate equation forces independent support under gamma>1, while a cyclic invertible linear recurrence proves uniqueness of the positive point. Instability of nonalternating support is witnessed by a decoupled scalar logistic perturbation. At even checkerboards the relative-cube linearized map is triangular with strict contractions and small higher-order terms. A circulant Fourier calculation gives the sharp odd-ring critical cosine and the strict exponential stability inequalities. At the critical boundary only neutrality and nonexponential attraction are claimed. The included executable passed exact rational candidate checks and finite spectral tests; finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The theorem classifies all 1+Lucas(n) equilibria of a clipped directed single-inhibitor logistic ring and proves the sharp size- and parity-dependent attracting-equilibrium census. Full accessible primary texts concern random heterogeneous couplings, undirected competitive Ricker-type lattices, or two-site symmetric coupling, so none proves or subsumes this support and spectral theorem.

No independent human validation or exhaustive review of the global competitive-map literature has been performed.

value.rationale: This is a motivated complete all-size fixed-point classification of a natural directed inhibitory counterpart to a recently studied clipped logistic network. It uncovers exponential combinatorial proliferation of equilibria versus a parity-limited number of attracting fixed points, with an exact odd-ring inhibition window shrinking as n^-2. These facts are not a generic logistic-map one-site exercise and can inform deterministic pattern selection and frustration analysis in cyclic competition models.
